note: Attribution + reversibility record for migration 20260901160000 (REVIEW CAS-31). Two ERCOT yard complexes whose 345 kV secondaries HIFLD carries as 69 kV, forcing bulk transfer through 69 kV jumpers — exposed as the model's worst overloads (560 % / 201 %) the moment CEMS measured dispatch put real flow on them (REVIEW EXT-4). OSM shows neither site has the voltage level the flow was crossing at.

sites.name: North McCamey (Upton County, TX)
sites.correction: Bus 67745_69.0kV -> 138 kV (the LCRA yard is 345/138; its transformer becomes the real 345/138). Line 312659 (the 0.47 km inter-yard tie) -> 138 kV with re-estimated single-circuit parameters, AEP end re-pointed to 67972_138.0kV. Line 305583 (the 69 kV chain toward McCamey) re-pointed to 67972_69.0kV, so the local 69 kV system hangs off the AEP yard's HIFLD-asserted 138/69 transformer instead of the LCRA bulk yard.

sites.name: Eagle Mountain (Tarrant County, TX)
sites.correction: No 69 kV level exists anywhere in the complex (both repair lines and the yards' 69 kV buses touch nothing real). Bus 67652_69.0kV -> 138 kV; both synthetic repair lines -> 138 kV with re-estimated parameters, far ends re-pointed to the real 138 kV buses (69427_138.0kV, 71942_138.0kV). The 69 kV stub buses stay behind their transformers carrying nothing.
